summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease and a history of arteriovenous fistula complications was admitted for symptomatic steal syndrome in her right arm. She underwent a planned revision procedure—banding of the right arm arteriovenous fistula—to reduce blood flow and improve hand perfusion. The procedure was successful, with immediate improvement in hand pain and warmth. She tolerated postoperative recovery well, resumed hemodialysis without complications, and maintained stable vital signs and lab values. She was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor for access site complications, continue her regular dialysis and medication regimen, and follow up with her surgical clinic. Her warfarin dose was adjusted to 3 mg daily during the admission.
